title: Cold plasma technology as a novel antimicrobial platform: mechanisms, efficacy, and clinical translation: a systematic literature review

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Cold plasma technology as a novel antimicrobial platform: mechanisms, efficacy, and clinical translation: a systematic literature review》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0050】While several earlier reviews have addressed specific aspects of CAP – including hospital decontamination [6], disinfection technologies [7], bacterial load reduction [8], and biofilm interactions [9] – none have integrated recent mechanistic advances with a systematic comparison of efficacy across all major pathogen classes, updated clinical trials, biosafety, dosimetry, and economic considerations. Two recently published systematic reviews have further advanced the field by providing quantitative meta-analytic evidence for wound healing [10] and a comprehensive synthesis of dental applications [11]. The aim of the present review was to fill these gaps by providing a comprehensive, integrated, and up-to-date synthesis focused on AMR.

【Introduction · p0035】The relentless progression of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents one of the most serious threats to global public health, with recent estimates attributing nearly 5 million annual deaths directly to AMR [1]. The World Health Organization has repeatedly emphasized the critical need for novel antimicrobial strategies that operate through mechanisms distinct from conventional antibiotics [2]. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) technology has emerged as a particularly promising physical antimicrobial approach that meets this urgent need.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Cold plasma technology as a novel antimicrobial platform: mechanisms, efficacy, and clinical translation: a systematic literature review》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Method · p0060】This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines to ensure comprehensive and transparent reporting [12].

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We conducted a systematic literature search following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases (January 2018-December 2025). Included studies investigated CAP's antimicrobial properties in vitro, in vivo, or clinically.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Cold plasma technology as a novel antimicrobial platform: mechanisms, efficacy, and clinical translation: a systematic literature review》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Analysis of 64 included studies revealed that CAP's antimicrobial effects primarily stem from reactive oxygen and nitrogen species generation, causing oxidative damage to microbial membranes, proteins, and DNA. CAP demonstrates significant efficacy against multi-drug-resistant bacteria, viruses, fungi, and biofilms. Clinical studies show particular promise in chronic wound management, with randomized controlled trials demonstrating accelerated healing and reduced microbial load.

【Conclusion · abstract-4-1】CAP represents a promising multi-target approach to antimicrobial therapy, offering a multi-target mechanism that circumvents conventional resistance pathways. While standardization and dosimetry challenges remain, CAP holds immense potential for integration into clinical practice against AMR.

【Discussion · p0345】The future development of CAP technology will likely proceed along several parallel tracks: (1) Technologically, the trajectory points towards the development of flexible, wearable plasma patches for at-home management of chronic wounds, and the integration of real-time biosensors for closed-loop dose control; (2) Clinically, promising frontiers include the development of catheter-based plasma systems for treating endovascular infections, inhaled plasma-activated aerosols for respiratory tract decontamination, and its use in veterinary medicine to combat infections in livestock, thereby reducing agricultural antibiotic use; (3) From a commercial perspective, the development of disposable or single-use plasma devices could address infection control concerns while expanding accessibility. Because these applications differ substantially in technical readiness and safety requirements, their translation will likely occur at different paces, with superficial wound applications representing a nearer-term opportunity than endovascular or inhalational approaches.
